messages.author: f65cdebf441dbb1a
messages.subject: Error: c++ error: dpotrf failed
parts:
Dear colleagues,

we want to fit spatial occupancy models to some tiger data and get the above-mentioned error. Any idea what we did wrong ? Here is a summary of input data set, the detection model (which seems to cause the trouble) and the detailed error message.

# Data set
List of 4
 $ y       : num [1:1202, 1:9] 0 1 0 0 1 0 0 0 1 1 ...
 $ occ.covs: num [1:1202, 1:60] 0.825 0.879 1.003 0.715 0.825 ...
  ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  .. ..$ : chr [1:1202] "1" "2" "3" "4" ...
  .. ..$ : chr [1:60] "occ.covs.zele_4000m" "occ.covs.zele_4000m2" "occ.covs.ztemp_250m" "occ.covs.ztemp_250m2" ...
 $ det.covs:List of 3
  ..$ mon1  : num [1:1202, 1:9] -1.46 -1.46 -1.46 -1.46 -1.46 ...
  ..$ mon2  : num [1:1202, 1:9] 2.13 2.13 2.13 2.13 2.13 ...
  ..$ effort: num [1:1202] 0.0975 -0.3976 -0.3976 -0.2626 -0.3076 ...
 $ coords  : num [1:1202, 1:2] 233462 238512 238723 241837 242195 ...

# det.formula
~mon1 + mon2 + effort

# Detailed error output
Fehler in spPGOcc(occ.formula = occ.formula, det.formula = det.formula,  :
  c++ error: dpotrf failed

Thanks for your help, best regards --- Marc

messages.author: 5df889d339ff56a5
messages.subject: Re: Error: c++ error: dpotrf failed
parts:
Hi Marc,

This error can occur if you have sites with identical coordinates. Check to see if this is the case. If you do have duplicate coordinates but still want to include all sites, you can try slightly adjusting the duplicate coordinates by adding a few centimeters to differentiate their geographic positions—this solution has worked for me. Alternatively, you could remove the sites with duplicate coordinates.

Cheers,
José
